Ramniwas Dhakare vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 July,
2025
 Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Gwl:14348

 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh

At Gwalior
 Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Deepak Khot
 On The 11 th Of July, 2025
 Misc. Appeal No. 7349 of 2023
 Ramniwas Dhakare
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh
 Appearance:

Shri Deependra Singh Raghuwanshi - Advocate for the appe
 Shri Naval Kishor Gupta - Govt. Advocate for respondent/
 Order

The present appeal has been filed by the appellant challenging the order dated 18.10.2023 whereby,
the appeal filed under Section 70 of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and an application under Section 5 of the Limitation Act have been dismissed on account of delay.

2. It is submitted by the learned counsel for the appellant that the learned appellate Court did not consider the ground of the delay and only on the point of appellant's negligence to prosecute the proceedings remanded before the Executive Magistrate-cum-Adjudicating Officer has rejected the appeal as matter remained pending before the adjudicating officer from 29.01.2021 to 28.03.2023 till the decision has been rendered.

It is opined by the learned court below that despite there being an order in favour of the appellant for fresh adjudication by the competent authority vide order dated 29.1.2021, the appellant remained absent before the adjudicating officer for about two years and on the point of his lithargy, negligence and conduct the appeal has been dismissed.
It is submitted by the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:14348 2 MA-7349-2023 counsel for the appellant that no analysis has been done by the learned court below of the delay in filing the appeal.

It is submitted by the counsel for the appellant that the affidavit has been submitted in support of Section 5 but without conducting any inquiry on the question of delay, the appeal has been dismissed in a cursory manner only discussing the negligence and conduct of the appellant before the adjudicating officer.
It is submitted that the appeal was filed with the delay of about 3 months as the decision has been taken by the adjudicating officer on 28.03.2023 and the appeal was submitted on 26.06.2023.

The limitation prescribed for filing the appeal is 30 days and as such there was 60 days delay in filing the appeal, but learned appellate court without considering the fact Ramniwas Dhakare vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65548565/

sentences.text:
1 of delay has instead dismissed the appeal on the conduct and negligence as held by the appellate court before the adjudicating officer and therefore, prayed that a chance be given to the appellant to atleast submit his case before the adjudicating officer in compliance of the remand order.
3.
Refuting the submissions made by the appellant, the counsel for the State submitted that the order is just and proper.
The appellant was lethargic and negligent in prosecuting his case and therefore, the appellate authority has rightly rejected the appeal on the ground of delay.

It is submitted that despite of the remand order the appellant did appear before the adjudicating officer on a date but thereafter remained absent which shows that the appellant has no respect for the orders of the Court and prayed that the appeal be dismissed on this ground itself.

4. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
5.

It is evident from the bare perusal of the order dated 18.10.2023 passed by the appellate court that the appellate court in his discretion only has emphasised on the conduct of the appellant before the adjudicating authority by not appearing after 24.02.2021.

It is submitted by the counsel for the appellant that NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:14348 3 MA-7349-2023 because he was not aware of the legal procedure, he did appear on the date specified but he was not given proper dates and information regard to case, he remained absent.

Therefore, he was not aware when the adjudicating officer has passed an order but when he went to the court for his other work he was informed that the case pending before the adjudicating authority has been finally decided vide order dated 28.03.2023.
6.

It is also seen that the learned court below did not opine that the delay in filing the appeal was bonafide or not, in fact on Section 5, no findings have been recorded by the appellate court.
7.

Therefore, in the interest of justice, this Court deems it appropriate to remand the matter back to the appellate authority by condoning the delay in filing the appeal before the appellate authority to decide the case on its own merits considering the record of the adjudicating authority and other material.
Accordingly, appeal stands allowed.
No order as to cost.
8. It is observed that the appellant shall appear on 13.08.2025 before the appellate authority and prosecute the appeal diligently and no adjournment shall be sought by the appellant.
In case, any lethargy or negligency shown by the appellant before the appellate authority, the appellate court is free to pass appropriate order in accordance with law.
